record.hypothesis: A nominal u64 region-count bound can safely size dense temporary indexes before canonicalization.
record.attempted_change: Retain region_count-sized region dependency and renumbering arrays while admitting raw logical records and canonical wire records.
record.observed_outcome: An independently constructed 97-byte BPI2 image declaring the maximum u64 nominal region count terminated the native checker with SIGABRT and an integer-overflow panic inside ArenaAllocator.

source_refs.summary: Exact malformed bytes, failing executable digest and observed native failure.
Malformed wire rejection and valid unused-name normalization regressions.
A used region name near u64 max normalizes to the same canonical image as region zero.

falsifying_evidence: 97-byte input sha256 7a781d4dd78b07a85ed7877c1c10824295f42a1fab38f6af2967a942fa024248 caused an allocator integer-overflow panic.
The numeric upper bound denotes available names, not a materialized collection length.
record.exclusion_rule: Do not size region indexes from the nominal region_count bound before canonicalization when sparse or unused names are admitted.
applicability_conditions: Region IDs are nominal u64 ordinals and region_count is their upper bound.
Untrusted wire or native logical inputs may carry sparse or unused names before canonical checking.
Temporary allocation width is derived from region_count rather than referenced region IDs.

reopening_criteria.condition: The index domain is derived from materialized/referenced regions and malformed maximum counts plus valid sparse/unused-name counterparts pass without an ordinal-sized allocation.

record.next_search_hint: Keep dense indexing for actual stored catalogs; use a sparse nominal-ID map where the integer is only a namespace bound.
record.surface: Temporary region dependency and canonical-renumbering indexes
record.artifact_state_label: Native ReleaseSafe test executable that crashed on the maximum nominal region count

record.hypothesis: The entire captured context plus successor argument and state can represent the resumed body result when transferring return-clause borrow constraints.
record.attempted_change: Reuse initial-handler return requirements at resume_with and approximate the returned body value by all borrows in its token, argument and state.
record.observed_outcome: The first shared return-input implementation rejects the valid older capability returned by the resumed body. The unchanged predecessor compiles it and native World reaches Yielded. Both versions preserve the direct initial-handler counterpart.

source_refs.summary: The body and pair variants preserve older returned references while rejecting younger selected references, for initial and successor handlers and delegated writers.
Immutable failed source and before/after observation digests.
Predecessor admits the required-valid older returned-body case.

falsifying_evidence: Original public source probe sha256:570db1d1908e1526bb57ed8c5ce64f89d852e7594a1b65cab2e4ecadc811b6e8; predecessor output sha256:f119c02c94433ca7e0b402a18e709043584356b15905c06430bfdacf6aead6a9; failed-candidate output sha256:312aa8142fec227983ccf52238141160334d48aedf860dbd9efcbf8035d9a000.

An older capability returned by the body and stored in an older cell is valid even when the captured control also retains a younger handler capability. Whole-capture projection incorrectly rejects it.
record.exclusion_rule: Do not substitute every captured borrow for the selected resumed-body result when enforcing successor return-clause cell-write lifetimes in this admission model.
applicability_conditions: Return functions may write a selected body result into a cell.
Valid captures may contain younger references unrelated to the returned value.
The accepted domain preserves older returned references, including one selected field of a mixed-age product.

reopening_criteria.condition: The replacement projection traces the selected returned value through actual captured code and saved state, and preserves the older body and product-field regressions without admitting younger writes.

record.next_search_hint: Reuse the existing returned-value flow and saved-frame delivered projection with the result selector retained.
